about: Stepping through a real review (the Opera Game, engine line off), the sentence's standing clause never disagrees in category with the eval bar at any ply, and a ply whose stored evaluation is removed from the cache gets no standing clause at all. Graded by gate 234 (TC-R399, TC-R400) at kunal761 and 320x568; gate 21's TC-R87 keeps the unit layer. NOT COVERED: the folded cost-in-chances wording (Kunal's Desk answer of 11 Oct, whose render he must see before main; the batch 13 sentences have since removed the pawns-of-advantage clause) and the folded sacrifice sentence's second pawn (TC-R113 covers the trade rule).

breaks.name: a-missing-eval-reads-as-level
breaks.why: rtStand treats a missing evaluation as 0 again, so the unanalysed ply reads 'The game is about even.' - the job's defect

breaks.name: the-standing-names-the-wrong-side
breaks.why: the standing clause names the other side as better (a sign error between the stored analysis and the words)

breaks.name: the-standing-reads-pawns-as-centipawns
breaks.why: the standing clause divides a pawn value by 100 (the #385 scale error), so every ply reads 'about even' beside a bar that is not
